descriptor: BNPL lender funding a customer receivables book · reported in AUD

sections.title: Growth & Profitability
sections.subtitle: FY22-FY25 net income carries large one-offs (impairment, discontinued ops, note gain, tax benefit) -- see the Profit and FCF chart notes

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
charts.annotation: Net income includes one-offs: FY22 ~A$821m goodwill/intangibles impairment (failed UK/EU expansion), FY23 ~A$41m discontinued-operations loss, FY24 ~A$140m gain on convertible note extinguishment, FY25 ~A$55m deferred-tax-asset recognition benefit. Operating income is the cleaner read on the underlying trend.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal. Net income also carries large one-offs across recent years: FY22 ~A$821m goodwill/intangibles impairment (failed UK/EU expansion), FY23 ~A$41m discontinued-operations loss, FY24 ~A$140m gain on convertible note extinguishment, and FY25 ~A$55m deferred-tax-asset recognition benefit -- none of these are organic operating trends, and the FY24-25 swing back to profitability is driven largely by the note gain and tax benefit rather than underlying margin expansion.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Zip Co Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted). The restricted slice is cash pledged as collateral to Zip's warehouse funding facilities, which finance the receivables book -- it is not available for corporate use even though it sits on the balance sheet as cash.

For Zip Co Limited: total debt here is dominated by warehouse facility drawdowns and corporate notes that fund the loan book, not conventional corporate borrowing -- it should be read alongside Customer Receivables, not against operating cash flow alone. Restricted cash has grown from ~A$41m (FY21) to over A$225-370m in recent periods as the funding structure has scaled.

What to watch:

  • Restricted cash as a share of total cash (funding-facility intensity)
  • Total debt growing in line with receivables, not faster
  • Warehouse facility refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Zip Co Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Zip Co Limited: reported operating cash flow swings with the growth (or run-off) of the customer receivables book -- a growing loan book consumes cash even in a profitable period, which is why OCF was negative in FY2025/FY2026 despite positive net income. Net income itself has been distorted by large one-offs almost every year since FY2022 (impairment, discontinued-ops loss, note-extinguishment gain, tax benefit) -- treat any single year's net income as noisy and look at multi-year trend and the underlying/segment disclosures in the filings instead.

What to watch:

  • OCF driven by receivables growth versus genuine cash generation
  • Net income containing one-off gains/losses not present in cash flow
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Zip Co Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Zip Co Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

receivables.title: Customer receivables (loan book)
receivables.content:
Customer receivables is the outstanding balance of Zip's BNPL loan book -- the amount customers owe across all instalment plans, before impairment provisions. It is the core asset a lender like Zip funds, prices and collects against, analogous to a bank's loan portfolio.

For Zip Co Limited: the book roughly doubled from ~A$1.1bn (FY2020) to ~A$2.5bn by FY2022 during the aggressive US/UK expansion, then plateaued through FY2023-FY2024 as growth-at-all-costs was abandoned, before resuming growth to ~A$3.0bn in FY2026 on a narrower, more disciplined footprint (US + ANZ). Growth here is what actually drives revenue -- it is funded by warehouse facilities (see restricted cash and total debt) and its credit quality drives impairment expense, which does not appear directly in this chart.

What to watch:

  • Receivables growth versus revenue growth (book turning faster or slower)
  • Receivables growth outpacing funding capacity (warehouse headroom)
  • Any renewed acceleration echoing the FY21-22 expansion that preceded the impairment

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Operating income deducts operating expenses from revenue; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Zip Co Limited: net income has been swung by a large one-off in almost every year since FY2022 -- a ~A$821m goodwill/intangibles impairment (FY22, failed UK/EU expansion), a ~A$41m discontinued-operations loss (FY23, exited markets), a ~A$140m gain on convertible note extinguishment (FY24), and a ~A$55m deferred-tax-asset recognition benefit (FY25). Operating income excludes most of these and is the better line for judging the underlying trend; treat the FY24-FY25 return to net profitability as partly one-off-driven rather than pure operating leverage.

What to watch:

  • Operating income trend versus the noisier net income line
  • Whether a given year's net income swing traces to a disclosed one-off

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Zip Co Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Zip Co Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
